name: How long does a kitchen addition usually take from start to finish?

mainEntity.name: How long does a kitchen addition usually take from start to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most kitchen additions take between three to six months to complete once physical construction starts, depending on scope and weather conditions. The timeline is split between structural work and interior finishing. Pouring foundations, framing the addition, and securing the building envelope typically take several weeks. Rough-in plumbing and electrical inspections follow before insulation and drywall can close the walls. The final phase involves detailed work: finish carpentry, cabinet installation, tile setting, molding, and interior paint. Unforeseen structural repairs or supply delays for specialized finishes can also lengthen project duration.
acceptedAnswer.description: Construction typically takes between 3 to 6 months, depending on structural scope, weather, utility rough-ins, and the time needed for finish carpentry and tile.
